subject: Access provisioning & admin controls — Stellara identity questionnaire

Subject: Stellara RFP — Identity appendix (questions)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Our security and identity team compiled an appendix with focused questions on SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and administrator controls. A few high-level asks:

1) SCIM coverage: Do you support SCIM 2.0 PATCH semantics (add/replace/remove), bulk operations, and does your SCIM endpoint preserve our 'externalId' and 'employeeNumber' attributes?
2) Provisioning model: Can you support both SCIM-based provisioning and IdP-initiated Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning? If JIT is used, what attributes are created and how do you reconcile against SCIM?
3) Account lifecycle: How do you handle suspended/terminated users — is there a state mapping (active/disabled) and support for immediate deprovisioning?
4) RBAC and admin delegation: What built-in admin roles exist and do you offer custom roles or scoped admin for teams (e.g., read-only support, billing-only)?
5) Auditing/retention: Audit log retention defaults and export integrations (Splunk/Syslog) — retention windows and export mechanisms.

I attached the appendix (Stellara_RFP_Identity_Appendix.pdf) with more context and a small spreadsheet we prefer responses to be mapped into. Would appreciate a consolidated reply by EOD Monday (6/22) if possible; our procurement team will ingest your answers directly into our sourcing tool.

Best,
Anika
Procurement Manager, Stellara Systems

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 09:15, Anika Shah <anika.shah@stellara.io> wrote:
> 1) SCIM coverage: Do you support SCIM 2.0 PATCH semantics (add/replace/remove), bulk operations, and does your SCIM endpoint preserve our 'externalId' and 'employeeNumber' attributes?

Short answers: yes / yes / yes. More detail below for their worksheet: 

- SCIM implementation: SCIM 2.0 core. We fully support PATCH operations (Operations array with add/replace/remove) and implement 'id', 'externalId', and all standard user-schema attributes. Custom attributes (employeeNumber, costCenter) are accepted via extension schema. We echo externalId on create and preserve it on update; externalId can be used as an authoritative key for matching.
- Bulk: We support the SCIM Bulk extension for batched creates/updates/deletes (configurable per-customer). For very large directories we recommend our bulk sync job which runs asynchronously and reports a bulk job status endpoint.
- Reconciliation/Conflict resolution: By default, SCIM is authoritative for account state when configured; we support configurable conflict policy (SCIM-wins or Redwoods-wins) per attribute. Reconciliation is time-ordered by lastModified unless configured otherwise.
- JIT vs SCIM: We support IdP-initiated JIT provisioning for both SAML and OIDC. JIT will create a minimal record (email, name, groups, externalId if present) and mark the source as 'jit' in metadata. If SCIM later syncs that user, the SCIM record will be merged using the externalId/email matching policy. If a SCIM provisioning job is configured as authoritative, it can overwrite selected attributes. We call this out in the mapping sheet we attached.
- Lifecycle mapping: We support 'active' (true/false), 'suspended' semantics via 'active' + custom 'accountStatus'. Termination can be immediate: SCIM DELETE will remove access at the next enforcement cycle (sub-second to seconds depending on route); for guaranteed immediate session kill we integrate with session revocation APIs to invalidate tokens.

I'll paste a short example SCIM PATCH snippet for their engineers if they want; also we'll include the mapping in redwood_scim_mapping.xlsx.

-Karthik

Priya / team — a few notes for the RFP response on logging and admin controls: 

- Audit logs: We capture admin actions (role grants, policy changes, user lifecycle events), auth events (successful/failed logins), and provisioning events (SCIM job status, PATCHs, bulk results). Default retention: 90 days. Enterprise tier: configurable retention up to 365 days (on dedicated/private deployments). Exports: we support streaming to Syslog, HTTPS webhook forwarding, and a native Splunk HEC integration. Logs can be pushed to customer-managed storage as well.
- Admin delegation & RBAC: Built-in roles: Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Support Admin, Read-Only Viewer. We support custom roles with fine-grained permissions (resource-level scoping by team/project). Scoped admins can be limited to a subset of projects or model routes. Role change events are audited and reversible.
- MFA and access controls: Admin-level MFA enforcement is supported; we also expose a role policy to require MFA for sensitive actions (e.g., key rotation).
- Session revocation: For terminated users we provide an API to revoke active tokens and a 'force logout' endpoint that can be called as part of deprovisioning flows.

I'll note these items in the spreadsheet under 'Audit & Admin Controls' and include configuration examples for their security team.

-Neha

Anika — thanks for the questions and the appendix. Please find our consolidated responses attached (redwood_scim_mapping.xlsx) and a quick SSO/SCIM flow diagram (redwood_sso_flow.svg). Key callouts: 

- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 supported with PATCH + Bulk; externalId and custom attributes preserved; configurable conflict policy.
- Provisioning: We support both SCIM and IdP-initiated JIT; JIT creates minimal accounts which are later reconciled by SCIM if configured.
- Lifecycle: Immediate deprovisioning supported; token/session revocation API available.
- RBAC: Built-in and custom roles, scoped admin capability, audited role-changes.
- Logs: Default 90-day audit retention; enterprise options up to 365 days and integrations to Splunk/Syslog.
